rows.title: The Road Dance
rows.evidence: It is set in the early years of World War I on the Isle of Lewis in the Outer Hebrides, where it was also filmed. October 2020 filming used Gearrannan Blackhouse Village, a restored village near Carloway on the Isle of Lewis.
rows.reject_reason: The article sets and films The Road Dance at Gearrannan Blackhouse Village near Carloway on Lewis. The photograph is the Callanish Stones. This row's own note says that is not a filming location and not a still from the film.
rows.summary: The Road Dance is set in the early years of the First World War on the Isle of Lewis, in the Outer Hebrides, and the article says it was filmed there as well. October 2020 photography used Gearrannan Blackhouse Village, a restored village near Carloway on Lewis.
rows.image_note: Photograph of the Callanish Stones on Lewis, not a still from the film and not Gearrannan.

rows.title: An t-Eilean
rows.evidence: The series is set in the Outer Hebrides. Principal photography took place on Harris in April 2024, with filming locations including Amhuinnsuidhe Castle.
rows.summary: An t-Eilean (The Island) is a Gaelic-language crime drama set in the Outer Hebrides. The article says principal photography was on Harris in April 2024, including at Amhuinnsuidhe Castle.
rows.image_note: Photograph of Amhuinnsuidhe Castle, a Harris location named in the article.

rows.title: Silent Roar
rows.evidence: Written and directed by Johnny Barrington, the film is set in the Outer Hebrides. Filming locations included the Isle of Skye.
rows.summary: Silent Roar, written and directed by Johnny Barrington, is set in the Outer Hebrides. The production note says filming locations included the Isle of Skye.
rows.image_note: Photograph of the Skye Bridge, on the island named as a filming location.

rows.title: 28 Years Later
rows.evidence: A community in the story has been subsisting on Lindisfarne, cut off when the causeway floods. The locations list includes Lindisfarne off the Northumberland coast.
rows.summary: 28 Years Later places a surviving community on Lindisfarne, cut off from Great Britain when the causeway floods. The article also lists Lindisfarne, off the Northumberland coast, among the filming locations.
rows.image_note: Photograph of Lindisfarne Castle on the island named as a setting and a filming location.

rows.title: Cave painting of the Crucifixion
rows.evidence: One of the island's caves contains a life-size painting of the Crucifixion, painted in 1887 by local artist Archibald MacKinnon after a dream. He restored it twice. It was vandalised in July 2006 and has since been restored again.
rows.reject_reason: The Island Davaar article describes Archibald MacKinnon's 1887 cave painting of the Crucifixion. The photograph is Davaar Lighthouse, and the row's note says the painting is not in the frame.
rows.summary: Island Davaar, at the mouth of Campbeltown Loch, has a life-size cave painting of the Crucifixion. The article says local artist Archibald MacKinnon painted it in 1887 after a dream, and that he later restored it twice. It was vandalised in July 2006 and has since been restored again.
rows.image_note: Photograph of Davaar Lighthouse. The painting is in a cave on the island, not in this frame.

rows.title: St Ninian's Isle Treasure
rows.evidence: The St Ninian's Isle Treasure, found on St Ninian's Isle, Shetland, in 1958, is described as the best surviving early medieval silver metalwork from Scotland. The hoard has 28 pieces, including twelve penannular brooches, and is now in the National Museum of Scotland.
rows.summary: The St Ninian's Isle Treasure is a hoard of early medieval silver found on St Ninian's Isle, Shetland, in 1958. The article describes 28 pieces, including twelve penannular brooches and eight bowls, and calls it the best surviving silver metalwork from early medieval Scotland. It is held by the National Museum of Scotland.
rows.commons_file: File:Early medieval hoard of Pictish silver objects dated c AD 800 from St Ninian's Isle, Shetland.jpg

open_image.attribution: National Museums Scotland, via Wikimedia Commons

rows.image_note: Photograph of the silver hoard.

rows.title: White Island figures
rows.evidence: Eight quartzite carvings are built into the ruined church wall. The article says they were probably carved between 800 and 1000 AD and later reused as building stones. The church and the carved figures are State Care historic monuments.
rows.summary: White Island in Lower Lough Erne has eight quartzite carvings built into the ruined church wall. The article says most of the figures wear the long tunics of churchmen and were probably carved between 800 and 1000 AD, then reused as building stones. The church and the figures are State Care historic monuments.
rows.image_note: Photograph of White Island in Lower Lough Erne.

rows.title: Lugnaedon Pillar
rows.evidence: Lugnad's stone, also called the Lugnaedon Pillar, bears the inscription Lia Lugnaedon Macc Limenueh. The article calls it the oldest Latin-alphabet inscription in Ireland.
rows.reject_reason: The Inchagoill article describes the Lugnaedon Pillar and its Latin inscription. The photograph is a landing beach. The file caption says it is not the main landing place, and the pillar is not in the frame.
rows.summary: On Inchagoill, in Lough Corrib, the article describes Lugnad's stone, also called the Lugnaedon Pillar. It bears the inscription Lia Lugnaedon Macc Limenueh, which the page translates as the stone of Lugnad, son of Limenueh. The page calls it the oldest Latin-alphabet inscription in Ireland.
rows.commons_file: File:A Landing Beach on Inchagoill - geograph.org.uk - 827841.jpg
rows.image_note: Photograph of a landing beach on Inchagoill, not a close view of the pillar.

rows.title: Runic writing in St Molaise's Cave
rows.evidence: Holy Island lies in Lamlash Bay off Arran and is the site of the hermit cave of the 6th-century monk St Molaise. The article says some runic writing is on the roof of St Molaise's cave.
rows.reject_reason: The Holy Island article says some runic writing is on the roof of St Molaise's cave. The photograph is the south-east lighthouse, not the cave or the writing.
rows.summary: Holy Island in Lamlash Bay, off Arran, is described as the site of the hermit cave of the 6th-century monk St Molaise. The article says some runic writing is on the roof of that cave.
rows.image_note: Photograph of the lighthouse on Holy Island off Arran. The runes are in the cave, not in this frame.

rows.title: Kildalton Cross
rows.evidence: The Kildalton Cross is a monolithic Celtic high cross in the churchyard at Kildalton on the island of Islay. It was probably carved in the second half of the 8th century and is often considered the finest surviving Celtic cross in Scotland.
rows.summary: The Kildalton Cross is a monolithic Celtic high cross in the churchyard at Kildalton on Islay. The article says it was probably carved in the second half of the 8th century, is closely related to crosses on Iona, and is often considered the finest surviving Celtic cross in Scotland.
rows.image_note: Photograph of the Kildalton Cross.

rows.title: Lindisfarne Gospels
rows.evidence: The Lindisfarne Gospels are an illuminated Gospel book produced around 715–720 in the monastery at Lindisfarne, off the coast of Northumberland. Eadfrith, bishop of Lindisfarne, is regarded as the scribe and painter.
rows.summary: The Lindisfarne Gospels are an illuminated Gospel book made around 715–720 in the monastery at Lindisfarne, off the Northumberland coast. The article treats Eadfrith, bishop of Lindisfarne, as the scribe and painter, and says the book is now in the British Library.

open_image.attribution: Eadfrith of Lindisfarne (presumed), via Wikimedia Commons

rows.image_note: Photograph of a Gospel incipit page from the manuscript.

rows.title: Book of Kells
rows.evidence: The article says the widely accepted view is that the Book of Kells was begun at Iona and continued at Kells, that it was produced by Columban monks closely associated with the community at Iona, and that the exact place of production will probably never be settled.
rows.reject_reason: The article says the exact place the Book of Kells was produced will probably never be answered conclusively, and lists a start on Iona as one of four competing theories. It does not establish that the book was made on Iona.
rows.summary: The Book of Kells is an illustrated Gospel book. The article says the widely accepted view is that it was begun at Iona and continued at Kells, and that it was made by Columban monks closely associated with the community at Iona. It also says the exact place of production will probably never be settled.
rows.image_note: Photograph of an incipit page from the Book of Kells.

rows.title: Grace Darling (Thomas Musgrave Joy)
rows.evidence: The Darling family moved to Longstone Lighthouse in 1826. On 7 September 1838 Grace Darling saw the wreck of the Forfarshire on Big Harcar from the lighthouse. The McManus Galleries hold three paintings by Thomas Musgrave Joy of her deeds with the Forfarshire, and a William Bell Scott painting at Wallington Hall depicts the rescue.
rows.summary: Grace Darling's family moved to Longstone Lighthouse in 1826. On 7 September 1838 she saw the wreck of the Forfarshire on Big Harcar from the lighthouse and, with her father, rescued survivors. The article says the McManus Galleries hold three paintings by Thomas Musgrave Joy of those deeds, and that a William Bell Scott painting at Wallington Hall depicts the rescue.

open_image.attribution: Thomas Musgrave Joy, via Wikimedia Commons

rows.image_note: Public-domain painting of Grace Darling by Thomas Musgrave Joy.

rows.title: O Columba
rows.evidence: MusicBrainz work 68b177bb-76cf-4a74-976f-499673bfb818 is titled O Columba, disambiguated as Inchcolm Antiphoner, 14th c., with the composer recorded as unknown.
rows.summary: MusicBrainz lists the work O Columba with the disambiguation Inchcolm Antiphoner, 14th c. The composer is recorded as unknown. That note places the chant in the 14th-century antiphoner of Inchcolm.
rows.image_note: Photograph of Inchcolm Abbey, the island named in the MusicBrainz disambiguation.

rows.title: Sanctorum piissime Columba
rows.evidence: MusicBrainz work 56c11bb7-0288-4d33-8def-b914df3f83ce is titled Sanctorum piissime Columba, disambiguated as In praise of St. Columba, Inchcolm Antiphoner, 14th c.
rows.summary: MusicBrainz lists Sanctorum piissime Columba with the disambiguation In praise of St. Columba, Inchcolm Antiphoner, 14th c. It is a separate chant from O Columba in the same 14th-century Inchcolm manuscript.
rows.image_note: Photograph of Inchcolm Abbey, the island named in the MusicBrainz disambiguation.

rows.title: Scattery Island
rows.evidence: MusicBrainz work 93b6dbd8-25bb-4406-83d5-0fb6bf7b2548 is a jig titled Scattery Island, with the composer recorded as traditional.
rows.reject_reason: MusicBrainz records only a traditional jig titled Scattery Island. The work record has no annotation or relation that places the tune on the Shannon island.
rows.summary: MusicBrainz records a traditional jig titled Scattery Island. The tune's name is the name of the island in the Shannon estuary, and the composer credit is traditional.

open_image.attribution: Charles W Glynn, via Wikimedia Commons

rows.image_note: Photograph of Scattery Island.

rows.title: The Dursey Sound
rows.evidence: MusicBrainz work bc1d91ca-e659-40d6-aa5b-4f403b9f3d4c is a jig titled The Dursey Sound, with the alias John Dwyer's, and names the Irish fiddler John Dwyer as composer.
rows.reject_reason: MusicBrainz records a jig titled The Dursey Sound by John Dwyer. The record does not place the tune on Dursey Island beyond the title.
rows.summary: MusicBrainz records a jig titled The Dursey Sound, also listed under the alias John Dwyer's. The composer credit is the Irish fiddler John Dwyer. The title uses Dursey, the name of Dursey Island and of the sound beside it.
rows.image_note: Photograph of Dursey Island.

rows.title: Gometra
rows.evidence: MusicBrainz work d3b921a9-d9d9-4eb7-bc50-dc1a308186e6 is titled Gometra. The composer relation names Fernie, described on that record as the Glasgow-based producer John Fernie.
rows.reject_reason: MusicBrainz records a work titled Gometra by the Glasgow producer John Fernie. The record has no note that places the piece on the island.
rows.summary: MusicBrainz lists a work titled Gometra and names Fernie, the Glasgow-based producer John Fernie, as composer. The title is the name of the island west of Ulva. The record has no longer note about the place.

open_image.attribution: Op. Deo at English Wikipedia, via Wikimedia Commons

rows.image_note: Photograph of the bridge between Gometra and Ulva.

rows.title: Davaar Island
rows.evidence: MusicBrainz work dc801a67-ee27-48da-99a5-d57245b52c60 is a song titled Davaar Island. The composer relation names Alice Thompson, described there as a pianist and composer.
rows.reject_reason: MusicBrainz records a song titled Davaar Island by Alice Thompson. The record has no note that places the song on the island.
rows.summary: MusicBrainz lists a song titled Davaar Island and names Alice Thompson, a pianist and composer, as the composer. The title is the island's name. The record has no longer note about Campbeltown Loch.
rows.image_note: Photograph of Davaar Lighthouse.

rows.title: Clyde Suite: III. Isle of Cumbrae
rows.source_title: Clyde Suite: III. Isle of Cumbrae
rows.evidence: MusicBrainz work 5f7c8d46-d6e9-469f-b476-08794a87c431 is titled Clyde Suite: III. Isle of Cumbrae, related as a part of Clyde Suite. The composer relation names Ron Moore, described there as a jazz guitarist.
rows.reject_reason: MusicBrainz only titles a movement Isle of Cumbrae, with no note that it is about Great Cumbrae. The photograph is a view of the Cumbraes from Goat Fell on Arran, not a photograph of Great Cumbrae.
rows.summary: MusicBrainz lists a movement titled Clyde Suite: III. Isle of Cumbrae, part of Clyde Suite, composed by the jazz guitarist Ron Moore. The movement name uses Isle of Cumbrae, the ordinary name of Great Cumbrae rather than Little Cumbrae.
rows.image_note: Photograph looking toward the Cumbraes from Goat Fell on Arran.

rows.title: Eel Pie Island Hotel
rows.evidence: The island had a club that was a major venue for jazz and blues in the 1960s. In 1956 trumpeter Brian Rutland started jazz sessions at the reopened Eel Pie Island Hotel. Arthur Chisnall then promoted jazz bands and, in the 1960s, rock and R&B groups.
rows.summary: Eel Pie Island had a club that the article calls a major venue for jazz and blues in the 1960s. Trumpeter Brian Rutland started jazz sessions at the reopened Eel Pie Island Hotel in 1956. Arthur Chisnall later ran the club and promoted jazz bands and, in the 1960s, rock and R&B groups.
rows.image_note: Photograph of Eel Pie Island.

rows.title: Enys Men
rows.evidence: The story is set on an island off the Cornish coast. Jenkin filmed Enys Men in West Penwith in spring 2021, and the article says he was inspired by Cornish landmarks such as the Merry Maidens.
rows.reject_reason: The island in the story is fictional. Filming was in West Penwith, on the Cornish mainland, and the article describes the film as inspired by local landmarks.
rows.summary: Enys Men follows a wildlife volunteer on an unnamed island off Cornwall. The article says it was filmed in West Penwith and inspired by Cornish landmarks, including the Merry Maidens. It does not name an atlas island as the set or the location.

rows.title: Mairi's Wedding
rows.evidence: The song is also known as the Lewis Bridal Song. John Roderick Bannerman, who wrote it, was born in South Uist and left aged seven for Glasgow. Hugh Roberton gave the English version the alternative title The Lewis Bridal Song in 1936.
rows.reject_reason: The alternative title Lewis Bridal Song does not say the song was made or set on the Isle of Lewis. Birth in South Uist, which the composer left at seven, does not place the song on that island.
rows.summary: Mairi's Wedding is also called the Lewis Bridal Song. The article says John Roderick Bannerman wrote it after leaving South Uist for Glasgow at the age of seven, and that Hugh Roberton gave the English version the alternative title The Lewis Bridal Song in 1936. It does not place the song on Lewis or on South Uist.

rows.title: Grabbers
rows.evidence: The plot sends a Garda officer to a remote Irish island. The fetched article does not name that island or a filming location on an atlas island.
rows.reject_reason: The remote Irish island in the plot is not named, and the article does not name an atlas island as a filming location.
rows.summary: Grabbers sends its characters to a remote Irish island that the article never names. The fetched page does not tie the film to an island in the atlas.

rows.title: Bannan (TV series)
rows.evidence: The series follows a return from Glasgow to the Gaelic-speaking island where the character grew up. The article does not name that island.
rows.reject_reason: The article says the story is on a Gaelic-speaking island and does not name it.
rows.summary: Bannan follows a return from Glasgow to the Gaelic-speaking island where the character grew up. The fetched article never names that island.

rows.title: Swallows and Amazons (1974 film)
rows.evidence: The children camp on a Lake District lake island which they call Wild Cat Island. The fetched article does not name Peel Island.
rows.reject_reason: Wild Cat Island is the name in the story. The 1974 article does not say the film was shot on Peel Island.
rows.summary: The 1974 Swallows and Amazons puts the children on a Lake District island they call Wild Cat Island. The fetched article does not name Peel Island or another atlas island as the location.

rows.title: The Northman
rows.evidence: Filming was in Iceland, the Republic of Ireland, and Northern Ireland, including Five Fingers Strand near Malin in Inishowen, County Donegal.
rows.reject_reason: Inishowen is a peninsula, and Northern Ireland is not an atlas island. The article does not name an offshore island in the atlas.
rows.summary: The Northman was filmed in Iceland, Ireland, and Northern Ireland, including Five Fingers Strand at Malin in Inishowen. Inishowen is a peninsula. The article does not name an atlas island.

rows.title: The Angels' Share
rows.evidence: The fetched article sets the story around a Glasgow community-payback group visiting a whisky distillery. It does not name an atlas island.
rows.reject_reason: The page does not name an atlas island as a setting or a filming location.
rows.summary: The Angels' Share follows a Glasgow community-payback group on a visit to a whisky distillery. The fetched article does not name an island.

rows.title: God's Creatures (film)
rows.evidence: The fetched article describes the film, cast, and reception. It does not name an atlas island.
rows.reject_reason: The page does not name an atlas island.
rows.summary: The fetched article on God's Creatures describes the film and its cast. It does not name an island.

rows.title: On the Isle of May
rows.evidence: MusicBrainz work acfcf061-64fe-42f6-937b-a9fba97b25ad is a song titled On the Isle of May. Relations name lyricist Mack David and arranger André Kostelanetz, and say it is based on Tchaikovsky's String Quartet no. 1. Nothing on the record places it on the Firth of Forth island.
rows.reject_reason: The title matches the words Isle of May, but the MusicBrainz relations identify a Mack David lyric set to Tchaikovsky, not a work about the Firth of Forth island.
rows.summary: On the Isle of May is a song whose MusicBrainz record credits Mack David's lyric and André Kostelanetz's arrangement of a Tchaikovsky quartet movement. The record does not connect that song to the Isle of May in the Firth of Forth.

rows.title: Brenda Chamberlain
rows.evidence: She won medals for Girl with a Siamese Cat (1951) and The Cristin Children (1953). Tide-Race (1962) is a memoir of life at Carreg on Bardsey Island, where she lived and worked from 1947 to 1962.
rows.reject_reason: Tide-Race is a memoir, which belongs with books. The named paintings are not said to depict Bardsey.
rows.summary: Brenda Chamberlain lived and worked on Bardsey Island from 1947 to 1962, and Tide-Race is her memoir of that stay. The paintings named on the page, Girl with a Siamese Cat and The Cristin Children, are not placed on Bardsey.
